title: Hinduism and Meditation: Tantra
scope: Oxford Handbook chapter describing meditation and visualization in major Hindu tantric traditions focused especially on Shiva, with explicit attention to liberation, ritual and pure-awareness practices.
limitations: Supports selected Shaiva/tantric traditions, not a universal claim that one meditation model is central to every form of Shaivism or Hinduism.

title: Theravada Buddhism and Meditation
scope: Oxford Handbook chapter on Theravada meditation, including Sri Lanka, bhavana, samatha, vipassana and the broader devotional/practical supports around meditation.
limitations: Describes Theravada traditions broadly; it does not identify a photographed mudra, date an object, or establish a historical borrowing from Shaiva practice.

title: The Ambivalence of the Hindus: The Buddha as Avatara of Visnu in the Mahapuranas and Beyond
author_or_institution: Bradley S. Clough; Journal of Hindu Studies / Oxford University Press
scope: Peer-reviewed historical analysis of the development, variety and ambivalence of the Vaishnava Buddha-as-Vishnu-avatar idea in the Mahapuranas and later tradition.
limitations: This is a Vaishnava theological reception of the Buddha, not Buddhist self-description and not evidence that Sri Lankan Buddhists generally understand the Buddha as Vishnu's avatar.

title: Murugan: A Tamil Deity
author_or_institution: Carl Vadivella Belle; ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute / Cambridge Core
scope: Academic chapter on Murugan in Tamil tradition, including repeated red symbolism and the name Ceyon/Seyon, 'The Red One'.
limitations: The chapter establishes the Tamil Murugan epithet and symbolism; it does not by itself show that red colour is a structuring ritual principle at either Nallur or the Kandy Perahera.
